newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's WEL Energy boosts year net profit by half.
newsitem.headline: NZ's WEL Energy boosts year net profit by half.

text.p: New Zealand's unlisted WEL Energy Group Ltd on Monday reported a 49 percent rise in tax-paid profit to $15.9 million for the year to June 30.
Chairman Brian Corban said the improved result stemmed from increased revenue, up nine percent to $101.7 million, and continued tight control on costs.
Return on shareholder's funds rose to 10.79 percent from 9.78. Directors recommended a final dividend of 31.1 cents per share, bringing total dividends for the year to 55 cents.

WEL said a total $9.9 million of the profit would be distributed to shareholders but earnings would be retained as a buffer to new risks arising from the New Zealand wholesale energy market which officially begins on Tuesday.
Power New Zealand Ltd and Utilicorp United Inc have about 48 percent percent of WEL, while 44 percent is held by the local WEL Energy Trust.
WEL's eight percent stake in Power NZ contributed $4.2 million in dividend income.
Chairman Brian Corban said demand in WEL's coverage area rose 5.34 percent, with 845 gigawatt hours of electricity moving through its networks during the year.
Increased demand was partially the result of growth of 3.1 percent in the economy of the North Island's Waikato region, the third highest rate in New Zealand.
Corban said the new electricity market presented both new challenges and greater risks for WEL, and it needed sufficient funds in reserve to manage these risks.

WEL was also concerned that changes to transmission costs announced by national grid operator TransPower would add significantly to costs, and it was negotiating with TransPower to try to contain the effect of the proposed rises.
